title: The augmented Koszul resolution computes the derived scalar-extension counit
statement: Let $A,S$ be commutative rings, $\varphi:A\to S$ a ring homomorphism, $r\geq0$, and $g_1,\ldots,g_r\in A$ a Koszul-regular sequence [def-weil-pbc-koszul-regular-sequence]. Put $I=(g_1,\ldots,g_r)$ and let $K_A(g)$ be the Koszul complex [def-weil-pbc-koszul-complex], with chain degree $q$ placed in cochain degree $-q$. Define $\epsilon_g:K_A(g)\to(A/I)[0]$ to be the quotient $A\to A/I$ in degree zero and zero in negative cochain degrees. This is a bounded finite free K-flat resolution [def-pc-module-kflat-complex] of $(A/I)[0]$, supported in degrees $[-r,0]$. Let $Q_A,Q_S$ denote the localization functors defining $D(A),D(S)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], and put $F(E)=\operatorname{Tot}(E\otimes_A S[0])$, with the $S$-action through $S[0]$ [def-pc-mixed-total-tensor]. For any left derived extension of scalars $(L,\eta)$ of this functor, with counit $\eta:LQ_A\to Q_SF$ as in [lem-pc-derived-tensor-second-factor-functor], there is an isomorphism $\alpha:LQ_A((A/I)[0])\xrightarrow{\sim}Q_SF(K_A(g))$ in $D(S)$ such that $$\eta_{(A/I)[0]}=Q_S(F(\epsilon_g))\circ\alpha.$$ No flatness of $S$ over $A$, properness of $I$, or nontriviality of either ring is assumed.

proof.text: By [def-weil-pbc-koszul-complex] and [lem-weil-pbc-exterior-power-free-basis], $K_A(g)^{-q}=\bigwedge_A^q A^r$ has the finite basis indexed by increasing $q$-tuples from $\{1,\ldots,r\}$, and is zero unless $0\leq q\leq r$. Every term is flat: tensoring an exact sequence with a finite free module is, in basis coordinates, a finite direct sum of that exact sequence, whose kernels and images are computed coordinatewise. The zero terms satisfy the same assertion. Consequently [lem-pc-module-bounded-flat-kflat] applies with upper bound zero and makes this complex K-flat, in the ordinary-module sense of [def-pc-module-kflat-complex].

proof.text: The differential into degree zero sends $\sum_i a_i e_i$ to $\sum_i a_i g_i$ [def-weil-pbc-koszul-complex]. Its image is precisely $I$, so the quotient map kills this differential; all other augmentation components are zero, proving that $\epsilon_g$ is a cochain map. Its degree-zero cohomology map is the identity of $A/I=\operatorname{coker}(A^r\xrightarrow{(g_i)}A)$. In negative degrees the source cohomology vanishes by Koszul-regularity [def-weil-pbc-koszul-regular-sequence]; in positive degrees the source terms vanish. The target has only degree-zero cohomology. Thus $\epsilon_g$ is a quasi-isomorphism [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] and, with step 1, the asserted bounded finite free K-flat resolution.

proof.text: Apply [lem-pc-mixed-tensor-pointwise-left-derived] with $R=A$, coefficient ring $S$, $f=\varphi$, and $N=S[0]$. In ordinary composition notation its universal counit has type $\eta^0:L_0\circ Q_A\to Q_S\circ F$ and is invertible on ordinary-module K-flat inputs. The universal properties of this pair and the specified $(L,\eta)$ give $t:L\to L_0$ and $u:L_0\to L$ with $\eta^0\circ(tQ_A)=\eta$ and $\eta\circ(uQ_A)=\eta^0$. Substitution gives $\eta\circ((ut)Q_A)=\eta$ and $\eta^0\circ((tu)Q_A)=\eta^0$; uniqueness for the respective universal pairs gives $ut=1_L$ and $tu=1_{L_0}$. Thus $t$ is invertible, and $\eta_P=\eta^0_P\circ t_{Q_A(P)}$ is invertible on every K-flat $P$. In particular this holds for $P=K_A(g)$ by step 1. The coefficient action is through $S[0]$, and no flatness of $S$ is required.

source.place: Tag 06Y6 (lemma-derived-base-change), K-flat computation; derived.tex Tag 06XN (lemma-find-existence-computes), followed by the elementary uniqueness argument for universal pairs.

proof.text: Write $K=K_A(g)$, $B=(A/I)[0]$, and $v=L(Q_A(\epsilon_g))$. Since localization inverts the quasi-isomorphism of step 2 [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], its image under the functor $L$ is invertible, so $v$ is invertible. Define $\alpha=\eta_K\circ v^{-1}$; step 3 shows that this is an isomorphism $LQ_A(B)\to Q_SF(K)$. Naturality of the specified counit at $\epsilon_g:K\to B$ says $\eta_B\circ v=Q_S(F(\epsilon_g))\circ\eta_K$. Composing on the right with $v^{-1}$ gives exactly $\eta_B=Q_S(F(\epsilon_g))\circ\alpha$. For $r=0$ the complex is $A[0]$ and the augmentation is $A\to A/(0)$; if $I=A$ the quotient is zero and the same quasi-isomorphism argument applies. The proof includes zero rings and imposes no properness or scalar-flatness assumption.
